executive_summary: Trend-Eyes gives the LEO harness a second set of eyes that keeps working when every seat is dead. The motivating case is the 2026-08-04 13-hour freeze: GHA crons kept firing while every seat-tick duty died, so nothing accumulated. The core split is OFF-SEAT EYES + ON-SEAT JUDGMENT — a GitHub Actions cron runs a mechanical trend SCAN and writes candidate rows; Solomon's seat GRADES those candidates on its existing crons and promotes at most one finding per day through the existing advisory lane. The cron never judges; the seat never has to be alive for detection. V1 delivers the detection spine: three trend classes (T1 REPEAT-QUESTION, T2 RECURRENCE-AFTER-FIX, T3 LESSON-DISJUNCTION drift), a candidate writer on the existing feedback table, a run-receipt so quiet-because-flat is distinguishable from dead-emitter, two-sided validation, and the GHA wiring that makes it actually run. Verification binds to the COUNTER, not the CALL: the nearest precedent (SD-LEO-INFRA-CONSULTANT-AGENT-PHASE-001/-002) reached COMPLETED having shipped two trend scripts that are verified UNWIRED, so a merged workflow file is explicitly not accepted as evidence here.

functional_requirements.title: Mechanical scan script with a pure-probe / injectable-resolver split
functional_requirements.description: New scripts/solomon/trend-eyes-sweep.mjs runs the daily mechanical SCAN. THE FILENAME IS LOAD-BEARING AND WAS CHANGED AT PLAN TIME (was trend-eyes-scan.mjs): the invocation classifier at lib/invocation-detector/requires-invocation.js:26 matches AUTONOMOUS_SUFFIX_RE = /-(?:loop|cron|sweep|sweeper|daemon|worker|autotriage)\.[cm]?js$/i and AUTONOMOUS_DIR_RE = /(?:^|\/)(?:cron|clockwork)\//i. A '-scan.mjs' name under scripts/solomon/ matches NEITHER, so classifyRequiresInvocation returns false and INVOCATION_PATH_PROOF would never see this script — the exact blind spot that let scripts/eva/eva-trend-snapshot.mjs and scripts/eva/trend-detector.mjs ship unwired. The '-sweep' suffix puts it permanently under the classifier. It follows the shape already established by lib/solomon/conduct-probes.js: pure probe functions that take facts and return verdicts, plus a separate injectable resolver that does the Supabase IO. This split is what makes the two-sided validation in FR-7 possible without a database. The sweep NEVER judges and NEVER promotes — it emits candidates only. It never messages the chairman (observe-never-join) and never gates anything (diagnostics only; tracesToLayer null). Auth is supabase-js + service-role ONLY: SUPABASE_POOLER_URL is injected into zero cron workflows in this repo and is silently undefined on a GHA runner (solomon-late-verdict-reconcile-cron.yml:38-40), so no pg/DATABASE_URL path may be introduced.
acceptance_criteria: scripts/solomon/trend-eyes-sweep.mjs exists and exits 0 on a run that finds nothing
node scripts/invocation-check.mjs reports requiresInvocation:true for the entrypoint — asserted by test, not by inspection
A loop-contract registry entry exists for the entrypoint as a second, name-independent anchor
Probe logic is importable and callable with injected facts, with zero Supabase access in the pure path
grep confirms no pg / DATABASE_URL / SUPABASE_POOLER_URL usage anywhere in the new code
The scan writes no row to any table other than feedback (candidates) and codebase_health_snapshots (receipt)

functional_requirements.title: T1 REPEAT-QUESTION — cluster inbound chairman SMS by question-class
functional_requirements.description: A chairman asking the same question-class twice across days IS a harness gap. Detection clusters inbound chairman SMS and fires on clusters with 2+ members at least 24h apart. Founding specimen: the SMS-coverage question asked 2026-08-03 and again 2026-08-05. The lane read reuses readChairmanSmsExchanges (lib/solomon/chairman-sms-exchanges.js:100), whose bounded window is MANDATORY — it throws on a non-positive windowHours (:102), so the scan must pass an explicit window. CRITICAL AND MEASURED AT LEAD: the clustering itself is NEW WORK, not reuse. The module's docblock at :43-46 states its correlation is chronological adjacency per counterpart phone, NOT similarity, and explains why it refuses similarity matching. The spine's listing of this module as 'reused, not re-derived' is true for the lane READ and false for the clustering; PLAN must not inherit the reuse assumption.
acceptance_criteria: Clustering fires on 2+ same-class inbound messages separated by 24h or more
Clustering does NOT fire on 2 same-class messages inside the same 24h window
The founding specimen (SMS-coverage question, 08-03 + 08-05) is a fixture in the test suite and fires
The scan passes an explicit windowHours to readChairmanSmsExchanges and never relies on the default

functional_requirements.title: T2 RECURRENCE-AFTER-FIX — read retention_archive UNION session_coordination
functional_requirements.description: A lesson-channel class reappearing after its fix ships is the T2 signal (live specimen: the sess-987 pointer writer). BLOCKING CONSTRAINT MEASURED AT LEAD (condition C1): session_coordination is a SURVIVOR table — 3,725 live rows spanning only 2026-07-24 to 2026-08-07, with 84% from the last 7 days. A trend computed on it measures the DELETION POLICY, not conduct. The codebase already states this at lib/coordination/answered-rate.cjs:3-8: 'READ THE LEDGER, NEVER session_coordination... a survivor-table rate measures the deletion policy rather than anyone's conduct.' The durable source exists and the SD spine does not name it: retention_archive holds 44,003 archived session_coordination rows spanning 2026-03-11 to 2026-08-06, populated by archive-before-delete (20260713_fix_cleanup_expired_coordination_where_clause.sql:38-42). T2 therefore reads the UNION of both. Zero-new-tables holds only under this union. Prior art to cite rather than re-derive: lib/learning/outcome-tracker.js:364 detectRecurrence already implements recurrence-after-fix at point-event granularity; the SERIES framing is what is new.
acceptance_criteria: T2 reads retention_archive UNION session_coordination, verified by a test that seeds a class present ONLY in retention_archive and still detects it
A recurrence whose only pre-fix occurrences fall outside the session_coordination retention window is still detected
The PRD-cited window spans more than the ~14 days session_coordination alone can carry
The implementation cites outcome-tracker.js:364 in a comment rather than silently duplicating it

functional_requirements.title: T3 LESSON-DISJUNCTION drift as a standing series, without becoming a fourth writer
functional_requirements.description: T3 tracks the ratio of lane-named-classes actually reaching issue_patterns as a standing series (Solomon measured 0-of-12 at 5c4da312). BLOCKING CONSTRAINT MEASURED AT LEAD (condition C2): issue_patterns.trend already has writers and T3 must not become another. calculate_pattern_trends() is live in pg_proc (20260110_pattern_intelligence.sql:55), performs 7d-vs-prior-30d trend detection over issue_patterns, has ZERO callers, and reads pattern_occurrences which has 0 rows — an instrument nobody invokes is indistinguishable from an absent one. Separately issue_patterns.trend IS populated (stable=1206 / decreasing=401 / increasing=38) by an unrelated age-based decay marker at scripts/detect-stale-patterns.js:104-120. T3 must either reconcile with those writers or scope away from that column entirely, and must say which in the implementation.
acceptance_criteria: T3 writes no value to issue_patterns.trend, OR the PRD-implementing commit documents the reconciliation with both existing writers
The ratio is emitted as a series reading, not a point verdict
A ratio whose numerator and denominator are measured over the SAME extent is asserted by test (no span mismatch)

functional_requirements.title: Candidate writer through the canonical feedback writer, honouring the insert contract
functional_requirements.description: Candidates persist as feedback rows with category=solomon_trend_candidate carrying self-describing queries in metadata, written through the canonical writer lib/governance/emit-feedback.js. Zero new tables, zero new transport. CONSTRAINT MEASURED AT LEAD (condition C4): feedback.category is genuinely free-text — varchar(50) nullable, not a pg_enum, and none of the 23 table constraints reference it — so the new category needs no migration. But feedback has four NOT NULL no-default columns (type, source_application, source_type, title), two of them CHECK-constrained (type in {issue, enhancement}; source_type in {auto_capture, ...}), so a naive writer takes a 23514 on its very first run. Additionally solomon_trend_candidate MUST be kept OUT of MACHINE_TELEMETRY_CATEGORIES (lib/governance/feedback-audience.js): membership routes a category through an aggregate UPSERT whose dedup hash is always today::telemetry::category, silently collapsing every row of that category into one per day and ignoring the caller's own dedup_key.
acceptance_criteria: Candidate rows are written via lib/governance/emit-feedback.js, not a raw insert
A test asserts all four NOT NULL columns are populated with CHECK-valid values
A test asserts solomon_trend_candidate is NOT a member of MACHINE_TELEMETRY_CATEGORIES
Two candidates from the same class in one day produce two distinct rows (not one collapsed row)
Each candidate row carries a self-describing query in metadata that reproduces its own finding

functional_requirements.title: Run-receipt per execution, with an external liveness reader
functional_requirements.description: Every scan execution writes a run-receipt so quiet-because-flat is distinguishable from dead-emitter. This pattern already exists and is named, and is copied rather than re-derived: scripts/gauge-runner.mjs:585-595 writeHeartbeat() inserts dimension=gauge_runner_heartbeat into codebase_health_snapshots with findings carrying ran_count/ran_at plus a routing tally; its header calls this 'Invariant #0 (who-watches-the-watchmen)'. The receipt is only half the mechanism — the other half is an EXTERNAL reader, because a receipt nobody reads cannot raise an alarm: lib/governance/gauge-runner-liveness.js checkGaugeRunnerLiveness is a pure predicate where a null heartbeat is alarm:true. Trend-Eyes copies the full triple: writer, table+dimension, external pure liveness predicate. Per the anti-Goodhart exploration floor, the receipt ALSO lists the top-N raw clusters even when they fall below threshold, so a narrowing of the instrument's vision is itself visible in the receipt series.
acceptance_criteria: A scan run that finds nothing still writes a receipt row
A pure liveness predicate exists, is separately importable, and returns alarm:true for a null/stale receipt
The receipt records a routing tally so dedup-suppressed-everything is distinguishable from the-scan-broke
The receipt lists top-N raw clusters below threshold (exploration floor)

functional_requirements.title: Two-sided ship validation in a single suite
functional_requirements.description: A one-sided test admits an instrument that can never fire. The suite must prove BOTH directions in the same run: a seeded known-trend MUST fire, AND a flat series MUST NOT. This applies per trend class, not once for the whole scan — a suite where T1's positive case carries the whole file lets T2 and T3 ship blind. Each class needs its own seeded-positive and its own flat-negative.
acceptance_criteria: For each of T1, T2, T3: a seeded known-trend fixture FIRES
For each of T1, T2, T3: a flat-series fixture does NOT fire
Both directions run in the same suite and both are required to pass
The negative fixtures are built on a different assumption than the positive ones, so a shared flaw cannot make both pass

functional_requirements.title: GHA cron wiring — proven by a real scheduled run, not by a merged file
functional_requirements.description: A new .github/workflows/ entry runs the scan daily, copying the canonical template .github/workflows/solomon-ledger-reconcile.yml (daily 06:00, concurrency group, dry_run input). Explicitly DO NOT copy solomon-judgment-expiry.yml — its schedule is commented out and it ships deliberately disabled. The template shape is: permissions contents:read; concurrency group=github.workflow with cancel-in-progress; ubuntu-latest; timeout 5-10m; job-level env with exactly SUPABASE_URL and SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY; checkout@v4, setup-node@v4 (node 22, cache npm), npm ci --ignore-scripts, one node step. THE ACCEPTANCE BINDS TO THE COUNTER, NOT THE CALL: the nearest precedent, SD-LEO-INFRA-CONSULTANT-AGENT-PHASE-001/-002, reached COMPLETED having shipped scripts/eva/eva-trend-snapshot.mjs and scripts/eva/trend-detector.mjs, both verified UNWIRED with no npm script and no workflow entry. The in-repo lesson is already written at .github/workflows/solomon-judgment-expiry.yml:22-25: 'that is not a disabled mechanism, it is an ABSENT one.'
acceptance_criteria: The workflow has an ACTIVE (uncommented) schedule
Ship evidence is a real executed run: a run-receipt row in codebase_health_snapshots with a timestamp after merge
A merged workflow file alone is explicitly NOT accepted as completion evidence
The workflow references only SUPABASE_URL and SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY

technical_requirements.title: Zero new tables, zero new transport
technical_requirements.description: Reads: sms_relay_staging, sms_outbound_obligations, session_coordination, retention_archive, issue_patterns, retrospectives, feedback, merge_witness_telemetry. Writes: feedback (candidates) and codebase_health_snapshots (receipt) only. No migration ships with this SD.

technical_requirements.title: Series mechanic reuses recursion-governor, not a new store
technical_requirements.description: lib/governance/recursion-governor.js already implements the append-a-reading / decide-from-the-sequence mechanic on the existing codebase_health_snapshots table: writeThroughputSnapshot appends per tick, fetchRecentSnapshots(supabase,{dimension,limit}) reads newest-first, detectSustainedBreach(recent,{requiredConsecutive}) returns {sustained, streak}. Reuse this rather than inventing a series store.

technical_requirements.title: Per-day promotion cap idiom already exists
technical_requirements.description: scripts/lib/ci-recurrence-detector.mjs supplies the cap idiom (DEFAULT_THRESHOLD, DEFAULT_PER_RUN_CAP, DEFAULT_PER_DAY_CAP). The at-most-one-promoted-finding-per-day rule reuses this shape rather than a new mechanism.

technical_requirements.title: Diagnostics only — never gates, never messages the chairman
technical_requirements.description: tracesToLayer null. The instrument gates nothing and acts on nothing (CONST-002). Findings reach the chairman only via the Adam packet; the scan holds no chairman-facing channel and must not acquire one.

technical_requirements.title: Narrow the no-existing-series claim in code comments
technical_requirements.description: The spine's global claim that no instrument owns longitudinal series is refuted (8+ exist; lib/ship/witness-adoption.mjs:131 already builds a day-bucketed 60-day series over merge_witness_telemetry, a source this SD names). The defensible claim, conceded by the gauge registry in its own vocabulary, is cited instead: lib/governance/gauge-registry.js:320 defines accumulationSignal as 'the alarm on the SERIES, distinct from the per-event signal', records it MISSING at :356 and :386, and states at :394 that 'only the series exposes the outage'.

risks.risk: The instrument ships and is never wired — the exact fate of the nearest precedent (SD-LEO-INFRA-CONSULTANT-AGENT-PHASE-001/-002, both COMPLETED with two verified-unwired trend scripts)
risks.mitigation: Acceptance binds to a real executed run leaving a receipt row, not to a merged file. FR-8 states this explicitly and the criterion is load-bearing.

risks.risk: T2 computes its trend on a survivor table and silently measures the deletion policy instead of conduct
risks.mitigation: FR-3 requires the retention_archive union and a test whose fixture exists ONLY in the archive, so a regression to the survivor table fails the suite rather than quietly returning a plausible number.

risks.risk: T3 becomes a fourth writer to issue_patterns.trend and corrupts a column three other things already touch
risks.mitigation: FR-4 forbids writing that column absent a documented reconciliation with calculate_pattern_trends and detect-stale-patterns.js:104-120.

risks.risk: The candidate category is later added to MACHINE_TELEMETRY_CATEGORIES, collapsing all candidates to one row per day while every test still passes
risks.mitigation: TS-11 asserts non-membership directly, so the collapse becomes a test failure rather than a silent loss of findings.

risks.risk: A one-sided test suite admits a class that can never fire
risks.mitigation: FR-7 requires per-class two-sided coverage, with negative fixtures built on a different assumption than the positives so a shared flaw cannot make both pass.

risks.risk: The scan swallows a query error into an empty result, making could-not-read indistinguishable from nothing-was-said
risks.mitigation: readChairmanSmsExchanges already throws rather than returning [] (lib/solomon/chairman-sms-exchanges.js:117-120); the scan must propagate rather than catch-and-continue, and the receipt records the failure.

metadata.v1_scope_boundary: V1 delivers the DETECTION SPINE (FR-1..FR-8). The self-improvement loop is deferred to a follow-on SD on a DEPENDENCY ground, not a convenience ground: the design specifies Tier-1 parameter learning as computed 'from recorded false-positive history' and bounded by 'precision drops two consecutive windows after a change', and neither the history nor the graded verdict series exists until this scan has run and Solomon has graded it. Tier 2 (class proposal) and Tier 3 (the weekly mirror) are marked in the approved design as follow-on rather than v1. The authority fence carries forward unchanged to that SD: the loop may learn DETECTION QUALITY only, never authority — it cannot add sources, change cadence or output surface, alter the admission tests, raise the one-finding-per-day cap, or touch anything chairman-facing, and all learned state lives in auditable, diffable, revertible parameter ROWS rather than code self-modification.
